read.bigIdea: You’re an ambassador of our brand.
read.where: Welcome to **Baldwin Restaurant Group, LLC (BRG)**. This training introduces our **core beliefs**, our **standards** and the high-level **philosophy of hospitality** that sets our restaurants apart. As a member of our team, you are not just an employee: you are an **essential ambassador of our brand**, helping us build **lasting relationships** with our guests and community.

hospitality: the art we set out to master.

read.bigIdea: Eight things we hold to be true.
read.where: Our values are things we **hold to be true**. Enforcing these beliefs determines **how we operate as a team** and how we succeed as an establishment.

read.bigIdea: Service is what you do. Hospitality is how it feels.
read.where: Understanding the difference between **service** and **hospitality** is the cornerstone of our success. To rise to the top, we must deliver **both**: exceptional service and genuine hospitality.
read.stopsTitle: As Danny Meyer writes in Setting the Table

stops.name: Service
stops.text: The **technical, transactional and logical** delivery of your product or task: handing someone a clean plate, pre-bussing, replacing silverware, fixing a billing error. Service is a **monologue**: we decide how we want to do things and set our own standards.

stops.name: Hospitality
stops.text: How the delivery of that product makes its recipient **feel**: the emotional connection formed when a guest feels truly **seen, welcome and valued**. Hospitality is a **dialogue**. It requires listening to the guest with every sense, then following up with a **thoughtful, gracious and appropriate** response.

read.mixup: **Service** is a monologue: we set the standard. **Hospitality** is a dialogue: it starts with listening.

sources: Baldwin Restaurant Group, Hospitality 101 Training (2026), page 1: Welcome and the core philosophy of hospitality.
